patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — GoTo Connect and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose GoTo Connect only if your buying job matches “Remote-team UCaaS phone system with meetings and messaging — Phone System / CX / Contact C” rather than Vonage's shape. Choose Vonage only if your buying job matches “SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/” rather than GoTo Connect's shape. Workflow advantage: GoTo Connect leans contact-center; Vonage leans sales-calling. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — GoTo Connect and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: GoTo Connect is Remote-team UCaaS phone system with meetings and messaging — Phone System / CX / Contact Center ladders are custom-quote (no public seat dol; Vonage is SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/Advanced higher..
- Company-size focus: GoTo Connect (small-business, mid-market) vs Vonage (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: GoTo Connect-leaning contact-center vs Vonage-leaning sales-calling.
- Researched limits: GoTo Connect — No published self-serve seat dollars — every plan is sales-quoted; Vonage — Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors.

Limitations — GoTo Connect: No published self-serve seat dollars — every plan is sales-quoted; Industry dollar ranges are low confidence and must not be treated as list prices; Vonage: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors; Call recording and deeper CRM land on Advanced / Premium packaging.

Poor-fit cases: GoTo Connect is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No published self-serve seat dollars — every plan is sales-quoted · Vonage is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors · Avoid GoTo Connect if you actually need Vonage's motion (SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
